subject: Seamounts
topic: There are more mountains under the ocean than anyone has ever counted.
script:
There are more mountains under the ocean than anyone has ever counted.
They're called seamounts: underwater mountains, most of them extinct volcanoes.
Some are flat on top. They're called guyots.
Their tops were once islands, flattened by waves before they slowly sank.
Scientists estimate there are more than a hundred thousand seamounts, and most have never been explored.
Their slopes push nutrient-rich water upward, which feeds an explosion of life.
Corals, sponges, sea stars and fish cover their rocky sides.
NOAA has explored seamounts from the Pacific to the New England coast, and found new species on many of them.
Which would you explore first?
